benefits.text: Wheat leaves a lot of residue on the ground: K-State calls it a large residue producer.
benefits.source: K-State, The Value of Crop Residue (MF2604, October 2003). https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/download/value-of-crop-residue_MF2604

risks.text: The long fallow stores little of the rain that falls on it: K-State reports that often less than 25 percent of the precipitation in the 14-month fallow between wheat crops is stored in the soil.
risks.source: K-State, Efficient Crop Water Use in Kansas (MF3066, August 2012), Fallow and Water Storage. https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/pubs/MF3066.pdf

benefits.text: K-State describes wheat-summer crop-fallow as more efficient in its water use than wheat-fallow, while calling the fallow period in both systems inefficient.
benefits.source: K-State, Efficient Crop Water Use in Kansas (MF3066, August 2012), Fallow and Water Storage. https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/pubs/MF3066.pdf

risks.text: K-State advises timing sorghum planting so that flowering avoids the hottest, driest period of summer.
risks.source: K-State Grain Sorghum Production Handbook (C687, revised May 1998). https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/pubs/C687.pdf

benefits.text: K-State describes wheat-summer crop-fallow as more efficient in its water use than wheat-fallow, while calling the fallow period in both systems inefficient.
benefits.source: K-State, Efficient Crop Water Use in Kansas (MF3066, August 2012), Fallow and Water Storage. https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/pubs/MF3066.pdf

risks.text: Under hot, dry conditions corn can be poorly or incompletely pollinated. K-State also puts the loss from one day of moisture stress in the week after silking at up to 8 percent of yield.

benefits.text: Corn is a high-residue crop, which helps keep the soil covered.
benefits.source: USDA NRCS, Nebraska Conservation Planning Sheet No. 4, Crop Residue Management (revised December 2006). https://www.mssoy.org/sites/default/files/documents/residue-mgmt-nrcs-2006.pdf

benefits.text: Soybeans fix their own nitrogen and normally need no nitrogen fertilizer.

risks.text: Soybean is a low-residue crop, so the ground has less cover after it.
risks.source: K-State, The Value of Crop Residue (MF2604, October 2003), which calls soybean a low residue crop. https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/download/value-of-crop-residue_MF2604 ; USDA NRCS, Nebraska Conservation Planning Sheet No. 4, Crop Residue Management (revised December 2006): residue from low residue crops provides less cover. https://www.mssoy.org/sites/default/files/documents/residue-mgmt-nrcs-2006.pdf
